newsitem.title: USA: CBOT oats rally to four-month highs on stocks talk.
newsitem.headline: CBOT oats rally to four-month highs on stocks talk.

text.p: CBOT oat futures rallied to a four-month high in the nearby March contract on talk of hampered movement of deliverable-grade stocks from Canada into the U.S., traders said.
"The oats are there, just not in deliverable position and we keep hearing talk they won't be delivered," a trader said.
There were rumors Tuesday that a rail car shortage in Canada would delay oat shipments to the U.S. from four to six weeks.
Traders said there was a lot of small commission house buying.
"Basically it was spec buying with some commercial selling in the May and July," he said.
March reached a session high of $1.86 per bushel, the highest level for that month since $1.86-1/2 was notched on October 10.
Oats closed unchanged to 8-1/2 cents per bushel higher, with March up 8-1/2 at $1.85-3/4.
"The market was short oats and now some shorts are covering and getting long. Technically it was a pretty good performance," the trader said.
First resistance for the March was at $1.81 and second resistance was at $1.91-1/4. The four and 20-day moving averages were giving off bullish signals for the market.
FIMAT Futures bought one million bushels of March, Dean Witter bought 300,000 bushels of March as did SAK Futures and Rand Financial bought 200,000 bushels of March, traders said.
Cargill Investor Services sold 300,000 bushels of March and Cargill Inc sold 300,000 bushels of July, traders said.
